archetype.name: Play-In Exit (one-star offense)
archetype.definition: A team that dug a 5-15 hole, climbed back behind Kawhi Leonard's All-NBA season to finish two games over .500, and went out in the play-in because the defense and the supporting cast never caught up to him.

report.headline: Kawhi's All-NBA year erased a 5-15 start but carried them no further

recap.finish: 42-40, third in the Pacific; lost in the play-in
recap.body:
This was a good offense attached to an ordinary team. The Clippers shot the ball as well as almost anyone, third in TS % at 60.2 and third in FT Rate, and still finished 16th in Net Rtg at 1.2. That number is the real verdict on the season. It is a long way from last year's 4.8 and 50 wins, and the 42-40 record and 19th-place site rank exactly match the 2021-22 team, which also won no playoff games.

The season split into a collapse and a recovery. November went 2-13, part of a six-game losing streak, and left them 5-15. December steadied at 6-6. January was the turn at 11-4 and put them at 22-25. February slipped back to 5-6, then March was the best month of the year, 12-6 while scoring 120.94 a game, which lifted them above .500 at 39-37. April went 3-3, and the last ten games went 6-4 with the wins and losses alternating: home wins over Toronto, Dallas and Golden State, and losses to Portland twice, San Antonio and Oklahoma City. They got back to .500 but never pulled away from it.

Kawhi Leonard is the story. He was first of 96 on the small-forward tab, scored 1,813 points on 62.9 TS % at a 33.5 USG %, and posted an 8 BPM and 9.2 Win Shares on his way to an All-NBA Second Team spot. His 14.5 On-Off is the clearest single number on the sheet. With him on the floor this was a very good team, and without him it was a losing one. He missed 17 games, and a roster that leaned on him this heavily had little margin for those absences. The wings graded B+ almost entirely because of him.

The rest of the roster is where the season went wrong. The backcourt graded D+ and the frontcourt D. Darius Garland played only 45 games. Kris Dunn played all 82 as a low-usage defender with a -0.8 BPM. Kobe Sanders and Cam Christie both had negative On-Off figures, and Christie shot a 48.4 TS %. John Collins was efficient at 64.3 TS % and led the non-Kawhi players in Win Shares with 4.6, but the team was worse with him on the floor (-3.9). The bigger problem was the glass and the defense. The Clippers were 29th in RPG and 21st in REB %. The defense fell to 18th after ranking 3rd last season, with a DRtg of 116.1 against 110.3 a year ago. A slow pace (96.5) also hid the offense: they ranked 11th in ORtg but 24th in points per game.

Luck did not decide this season, but it did not help. The margin implied 44 wins and they won 42, a W vs Pt Diff of -2. Even 44 wins from this group would have been a middling Western team. The play-in loss came from the 5-15 start and from a Net Rtg near zero, not from one bad night.

highlights.title: Kawhi Leonard's All-NBA season
highlights.body: Leonard ranked first at his position, scored efficiently on enormous usage, and was named All-NBA Second Team. His +14.5 On-Off shows the whole season ran through him. Every good stretch depended on his health and his volume.

highlights.title: Elite shot quality and free throws
highlights.body: The Clippers were third in TS %, sixth in eFG % and third in FT Rate, comfortably above the league on all three. This efficiency comes from how they hunt shots and get to the line rather than from hot streaks, and it has been stable for years. It is the most repeatable strength on the sheet, though the slow pace keeps the raw scoring totals modest.

highlights.title: The climb out of 5-15
highlights.body: After November's 2-13, the team went 11-4 in January and 12-6 in March to finish two games over .500. The recovery shows the team was much closer to average than its start suggested. It also shows how much ground the start cost them.

lowlights.title: Defense slid from elite to average
lowlights.body: The defense ranked 3rd a year ago and 18th this season, with DRtg rising from 110.3 to 116.1. Opponents shot well from three (21st in Opp 3P %), and shooting guards in particular scored freely against them. This drop, more than anything else, is why a 50-win team became a 42-win one.

lowlights.title: Beaten on the glass
lowlights.body: The Clippers were 29th in RPG, 21st in REB % and below the league on both the offensive and defensive boards. The frontcourt graded D. That leaves an efficient offense playing with fewer extra possessions than its opponents.

lowlights.title: Thin, part-time guard play
lowlights.body: The backcourt graded D+. Garland managed only 45 games, and the guards who filled the minutes mostly posted negative BPM and On-Off figures. With no consistent second creator, the offense depended heavily on Leonard.

arc.note: A 2-13 November sank them to 5-15. Strong Januarys and Marches pulled them back above .500, but a February dip and an even April left them short of a guaranteed playoff spot.

recap.nextYear: The carryover is Leonard and the shot profile. One elite wing plus the league's third-best TS % produced an 11th-ranked offense, and that should hold as long as he does. Collins' efficiency is real, even with his poor On-Off. Almost everything else needs work. The backcourt graded D+ and the frontcourt D, rebounding finished near the bottom of the league, and the defense lost the form that made it third-best a year ago. The -2 W vs Pt Diff means the true talent was closer to 44 wins, which is still a play-in team. The November collapse was too deep to blame on bad luck alone. Without better guards, size and defense, the 2025-26 numbers point to another season near .500 that depends on Leonard staying on the floor."

confidence.note: Full 82-game season. The sheet has no play-in game details, and the causes behind the November slump are not shown.
